caption.ru: Манипулятор удерживает рулон ленты двумя противоположными губками захвата, а молодой инженер в очках и свитере записывает результат. Редакционная иллюстрация к статье о PRISM Мичиганского университета: показан сюжет физического захвата, а не виртуальной ходьбы. Геометрия руки и организация рабочего места обобщены; это не точная реконструкция SO-101 или документальное изображение авторов опыта.
caption.en: A robot arm holds a roll of tape between two opposing gripper jaws while a young male engineer wearing glasses and a sweater records the result. An editorial illustration for the University of Michigan PRISM article, depicting the physical grasp experiment rather than simulated walking. The arm geometry and workspace are generalised, not an exact SO-101 reconstruction or a documentary depiction of the experiment's authors.
caption.ja: ロボットアームが向かい合う二つのつめでロール状のテープを保持し、眼鏡をかけたセーター姿の若い男性技術者が結果を記録する。ミシガン大学のPRISMの記事に対応する編集イラストで、仮想歩行ではなく実物をつかむ試験を題材にした。腕の形状と作業場所は一般化した表現であり、SO-101の正確な再現や実験を行った著者の記録画ではない。

alt.ru: Чёрно-белая гравюра: справа на лабораторном столе закреплена шарнирная роботизированная рука. Две соединённые с запястьем губки сжимают противоположные наружные стенки рулона ленты; отверстие открыто, под рулоном виден зазор и тень. Слева сидит молодой инженер в очках и свитере: правой рукой пишет карандашом на листе, левой придерживает бумагу. Фон белый, надписей нет.
alt.en: Black-and-white engraving: an articulated robot arm is fixed to the right side of a laboratory bench. Two jaws connected to its wrist grip opposite outer walls of a tape roll; its centre hole is open, with a gap and shadow beneath the roll. At left, a seated young male engineer wearing glasses and a knitted sweater writes on a sheet with a pencil in her right hand while steadying the paper with her left. White background, no lettering.
alt.ja: 白黒の版画。実験台の右側に関節式ロボットアームが固定されている。手首につながる二つのつめがロール状のテープの外側を左右から挟み、中央の穴は空いている。テープの下には台との隙間と影が見える。左には眼鏡をかけ、セーターを着た若い男性技術者が座り、右手の鉛筆で用紙に記録し、左手で紙を押さえる。背景は白く、文字はない。

visual_thesis: Точность работы управляющей сети проверяют конкретным физическим действием: захват удерживает рулон ленты, а исследователь фиксирует исход попытки. Сцена посвящена только физическому опыту из статьи PRISM; виртуальная ходьба и результаты других сюжетов не смешиваются. Губки касаются противоположных наружных стенок рулона; нагрузка передаётся через запястье, звенья и закреплённое на столе основание.
visual_brief:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create exactly ONE original landscape 16:9 editorial illustration for a robotics engineering newspaper. The single subject is the University of Michigan PRISM article: a laboratory robot arm picking up a roll of tape. This represents the physical grasp experiment ONLY, not the simulated humanoid walking test and not other stories. No collage, panels, diagrams or comparison scenes.

Style: mid-twentieth-century Soviet popular-science editorial engraving, modern robotics translated into black ink on a pure clean white background. Confident economical contours, expressive large black shapes, disciplined moderately spaced hatching and crosshatching for volume. Natural realistic harmonious human proportions, pleasant expressive face, restrained dignity of scientific work. Light face and hands, generous white areas, extremely readable when reduced for black-and-white newspaper printing. Entirely monochrome. No colour, sepia, toned paper, gouache, neon, decorative frame, political symbols, logos, letters, numbers, readable writing, watermark, UI or pseudo-interface.

Composition: slightly elevated three-quarter SIDE view of one sturdy uncluttered laboratory bench. A compact tabletop articulated robot arm occupies the right half, anchored with a simple flat base firmly attached to the tabletop. A plausible simple connected chain from base to shoulder to elbow to wrist reaches inward over the bench. Minimal functional links and clear joint axes; modest laboratory scale, not a massive industrial arm, not a humanoid. This is a generalized conceptual arm, NOT an exact branded reconstruction of SO-101 and not an assertion about the authors' detailed apparatus. Avoid decorative buttons, cables, handles, unused tools and elaborate mechanisms. Show enough of the bench supports for its stability to be evident.

CRITICAL PHYSICAL ACTION: one simple two-jaw opposing gripper at the wrist holds ONE ordinary plain roll of adhesive tape, its circular plane horizontal and its central hole clearly visible from above. The roll is lifted a small visible distance above the flat tabletop. Two short straight jaws descend from a common rigid gripper body and contact diametrically opposite OUTER sidewalls of the roll. The jaws squeeze inward from opposite sides; their gripping surfaces touch the roll clearly. The open space between roll underside and table must be visible, with a small shadow directly below. Roll is supported by friction at both jaw contacts, never floating unsupported. The central hole is empty; no extra finger through it, no hook, no floating tool, no handle, no loose tape strip. Keep both contact points visible from the chosen angle. Make the roll large enough within the foreground to read the two contacts at thumbnail size. Wrist, gripper body and both jaws form one connected causal chain back through the arm to its fixed base. No intersecting solids, detached joints, extra fingers or a jaw mysteriously attached to the tape.

Human: exactly one young adult male engineer, approximately 28–35, with short tidy hair, clean-shaven face, simple eyeglasses and a plain long-sleeved knitted crewneck sweater. He is seated on the left at a safe working distance and records the trial: his right hand writes with a pencil touching the paper, while his left hand steadies the sheet. Natural anatomy, professional concentration, no posing. He does not touch or support the robot or tape roll.

Background: almost empty white laboratory, only a restrained wall/bench context if necessary. No poster, monitor, furniture clutter or explanatory floating graphics. All details must explain the one experiment. Prioritize a clear supported bench, connected arm, two opposed contacts on the tape roll, and an unmistakable engineer recording results. A conceptual editorial engraving, not a documentary photograph, not a claim of commercial deployment or independently verified performance.

Revision instruction: Edit only the person on the LEFT of this existing black-and-white editorial engraving. Replace the woman with a handsome young adult male engineer, approximately 28–35, with short tidy hair, a clean-shaven natural face, and clearly visible simple eyeglasses. He wears a plain knitted crewneck sweater with long sleeves, no lab coat, no suit. Keep his seated professional working posture and exactly the same concrete action: right hand holds a pencil with its tip touching the paper, left hand steadies the sheet, concentrated attention on recording the experiment. Natural anatomy and realistic harmonious proportions, no posing. Preserve the robot arm, all robot joints, gripper geometry, BOTH opposing jaw contacts against the outer sides of the tape roll, the tape roll, its central hole, its gap and shadow above the tabletop, the table and the framing unchanged. Preserve black ink on pure white, bold contours, disciplined hatching, mid-century Soviet popular-science engraving style. No colours, logos, readable text, UI or extra objects. One coherent scene only; change only the person's gender, face, glasses and sweater.
